$description: Every token the engine proposes, and what people decided. The engine adds `proposed` lines (npm run tokens) and never edits a decision; a person or an agent makes each one `kept` or `cut` (npm run ledger -- cut <token> --why "…"). A cut token collapses to its fallback in every projection — semantic.css, tokens.json, the runtime — and every usage is logged by npm run validate. Nothing here is deleted: a stale decision about a token the engine no longer emits is reported, not removed.

--surface-page.reason: The house voice draws elevation as a wash and a rule, one level apart. Four levels is the order Visionary’s chrome already uses (ground, sunken, lift, overlay); fewer and a popover sits on the page it opens over.

--surface-sunken.reason: The house voice draws elevation as a wash and a rule, one level apart. Four levels is the order Visionary’s chrome already uses (ground, sunken, lift, overlay); fewer and a popover sits on the page it opens over.

--surface-raised.reason: The house voice draws elevation as a wash and a rule, one level apart. Four levels is the order Visionary’s chrome already uses (ground, sunken, lift, overlay); fewer and a popover sits on the page it opens over.

--surface-overlay.reason: The house voice draws elevation as a wash and a rule, one level apart. Four levels is the order Visionary’s chrome already uses (ground, sunken, lift, overlay); fewer and a popover sits on the page it opens over.

--surface-veil.reason: A dialog on a veil is the one place the grammar dims the page. Without it the backdrop competes with the sheet.

--ink.reason: Ink is the accent when the theme is monochrome, so it is the most-used colour in the system.

--ink-muted.reason: One family, so hierarchy is weight, size and ink strength. Three strengths of ink is the whole secondary/tertiary vocabulary; the portfolio is set in exactly these three.

--ink-faint.reason: The label colour. Every kicker, key and rule-line is faint ink, never the accent — a coloured label is a second voice.

--ink-inverse.reason: Text on a filled action. When the accent is ink, the label on it is the page colour; that pair is the monochrome button.

--accent.reason: Monochrome by default is not the absence of an accent — it is an accent compiled to ink. The gate stays open because colour is a choice the seeds can still make, and one filled action per surface needs one colour to be filled with.

--accent-strong.reason: The one hover step a filled action gets. Cutting it left a primary button that answered a hover with nothing at all, which reads as a dead control.

--accent-ink.reason: The label on the accent. Derived by the engine so a chromatic accent still carries a readable label.

--accent-soft.reason: The wash is the hover on ghost actions and the selection tint — Visionary’s --sel. It is the accent’s only appearance on a surface.

--accent-line.reason: A tinted rule for the one selected thing. Everything else is drawn in --line.

--line.reason: The grammar draws with lines: every card, row, panel and ledger is a 1px rule. This is the most-used non-ink token and the thing shadows were cut in favour of.

--line-strong.reason: The rule for an edge that has to hold on its own — a panel border, a table head. One step, not a scale.

--focus-ring.reason: Keyboard focus stays visible in every theme. Not a taste question.

--positive.reason: Status is ink and a word; the colour confirms, never carries. Kept because a status that is only text is slower to scan in a console.

--danger.reason: As positive. Danger is never only a colour.

--positive-soft.reason: The wash behind a status badge. The badge is a filled pill, so it needs one fill that is not the ink.

--shadow-color.reason: Lines, not shadows. The reference grammar — the portfolio and Visionary alike — draws every level with a 1px rule and an alpha wash, and paints no drop shadow anywhere; a shadow is decoration the eye pays for on every card. The elevation tokens keep their offsets and paint nothing, so the rule does the work it was already doing.

--motion-fast.reason: Hover and focus. Visionary’s chrome answers in 120–160ms.

--motion-base.reason: A sheet or a toast entering.

--motion-slow.reason: The ground changing. A theme flip is the one slow transition the site has, and it should be seen.

--motion-ease.reason: One curve, an ease-out, the way the portfolio’s --ease is one curve.

--motion-ease-emphasis.reason: Nothing bounces. The engine gives a calm theme a spring on emphasis above energy 0.3, and a dialog that overshoots is a personality the chrome should not have. Collapses to the ordinary curve; the energy dial still sets speed.

--density.reason: Density is a dial the owner of a screen turns, not a taste. Kept at 1.

--radius-interactive.reason: A control rounds a little — 6–8px at calm energy — so a row of them reads as instruments rather than boxes.

--radius-surface.reason: A panel rounds a little more than a control. The portfolio’s panels are 10px; this compiles to 12px at the house energy.

--radius-overlay.reason: Two radii, not three: a control and a panel. The engine gave overlays 2.4× the control radius, which at calm energy is a 19px dialog — the one soft shape on an otherwise architectural page. An overlay is a panel; it rounds like one.
